Review Sentiment

A natural-language-processing pipeline that reads 10,000 Yelp restaurant reviews and labels each one as positive, neutral or negative.

GitHub ↗
10,000Reviews
84.1%Accuracy
4Models compared
3Classes

Overview

Restaurants receive far more reviews than anyone can read. This project trains a classifier on 10,000 English Yelp restaurant reviews to label each one positive, neutral or negative, and ships it as a small app for single or batch predictions.

Approach

  • Converted the reviews into TF-IDF features.
  • Compared Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, SVM and class-balanced variants, choosing the final model by macro F1 so the smaller neutral class counts as much as the others.
  • Tuned hyperparameters with cross-validation.
  • Studied the errors with confusion matrices and per-class F1 to address class imbalance.
  • Reached 84.1% accuracy on the test set.

The app

The app has three parts: Analyze scores a single review and shows the probability for each class; Batch scores one review per line and summarises the distribution; Model report carries the training diagnostics — class balance, model comparison, word clouds per class and per-class F1.
